Landing pages and websites

Landing pages and websites built by the person who runs the ads, so the page and the campaign are one decision

Most of the waste in a PPC account happens after the click, on a page the person running the ads has never been allowed to touch. Here the page is in scope: written to the ad that sends the traffic, built on your CMS or as a static page, tracked before it goes live, and tested against a control until it earns its place. When the site itself is the problem, a 5 to 8 page business website is in scope too, with hosting, consent and the paperwork handled, so what lands on your desk is a brief to answer and copy to approve.

Why the page is part of the campaign

Message match

The ad promised emergency boiler repair in Croydon; the page says "welcome to our plumbing company". Every mismatch is paid for twice: in the click and in the Quality Score of the next one.

One page per intent

Not per campaign, not per keyword, per intent. An audit page, a management page, a "switching from an agency" page. Twelve services on one page is a brochure, not a landing page.

Speed and forms

Under two seconds on a phone, a form that asks for what qualifies the enquiry and nothing more, phone tracking that knows which keyword rang.

Tracked before it is live

The page ships with its GA4 events, Tag Manager triggers and conversion actions already tested. A page that goes live untracked has wasted its first week of data.

What is delivered

  • Copy. Written from the search terms and the sales conversations, not from the brand deck. Headline, proof, offer, form, objections, in that order.
  • Build. Hand coded HTML, as fast static pages on your domain or on a subdomain you control, with or without hosting by me. No WordPress, no page builder. Your design system is respected; no new brand is invented.
  • Website. When the current site cannot carry the campaign, five to eight pages: home, services, about, proof and contact, plus what a buyer reads before calling. Built for the campaigns rather than for a portfolio, as hand coded HTML pages that load fast and have no CMS to maintain. Online shops and brand identity work are not included.
  • Tracking. Form, phone, chat and booking events wired into GA4, Tag Manager and the ad platforms, with enhanced conversions, the Meta Conversions API and Consent Mode v2 for UK and EU visitors.
  • Test plan. One control, one challenger, one variable at a time, with the sample size worked out before the test starts so nobody calls it early.
  • Hosting and care. Static pages hosted under your domain on infrastructure I manage, with backups, updates, a monthly check that every tag still fires and an hour of changes a month, billed monthly. Or your existing host, if you have one.
  • Handover. The page is yours, editable by your team, documented.

The paperwork is mine

You answer a short brief and approve the copy. The rest of what a launch needs is my job.

  • Domain, DNS and SSL. Registered or transferred in your name, pointed and secured.
  • Consent and privacy. Cookie banner with Consent Mode v2, privacy page text in line with UK GDPR and PECR, and forms with spam protection that reach your inbox and your CRM.
  • Accounts connected. Google Search Console, Google Business Profile, GA4, Tag Manager and the ad accounts verified and linked.
  • Handover and invoices. Every login documented, code and content yours, and invoices in pounds that your accountant can file without a question.

Prices, published

Fixed prices for standalone projects, in pounds, ex VAT, with copy and full tracking always included. Inside a management retainer, building and testing pages is part of running the account, not a change request. Not a design agency: for a brand identity or an online shop I will recommend a specialist and work alongside them on the conversion path.

Questions people ask before hiring

Do you design the pages or just write them?

Both, within your existing design system. Layout, copy, build and tracking are done by me; original illustration, photography or a new visual identity come from a designer, and I will recommend one if needed.

Can you build on our WordPress or Webflow site?

The page itself is plain HTML, not a WordPress or Webflow page. It goes on a subdomain you control, or on your host, as static files, which are faster anyway. If it must sit inside your CMS, I deliver the HTML and your developer embeds it.

Do you build whole websites?

Yes, when the current site cannot carry the campaign: five to eight pages with the copy written, tracked from day one and hosted under your domain in the care plan. Online shops and brand identity work are not included, and I will say so rather than stretch.

Do you host it?

Optional, priced both ways. Without hosting you get the HTML files installed on your host. With hosting, the page lives under your domain on infrastructure I manage inside the monthly care plan, with backups, updates and a monthly check that every tag still fires.

How is it invoiced?

In pounds, ex VAT, or in euros for Irish businesses: £1,400 per campaign landing page, £450 per extra A/B variant, £3,900 for a 5 to 8 page website, £1,200 for a tracking setup on its own and £95 a month for hosting and care, as in the price table. Half on approval of the written scope and half on delivery, by bank transfer. No card payments.

Can an agency white label this?

Yes. The same page can be delivered under your agency's name with no mention of me, for agencies that run the media and need pages built without adding headcount.

Do you do conversion rate optimisation for the whole website?

For the pages that paid traffic lands on, yes, continuously. Whole-site CRO programmes are a different engagement and usually belong with a CRO specialist once traffic is large enough to test on.

How long does a page take?

Copy and build in three to five working days from brief, tracking tested before launch, and a first test result after enough traffic has been through it, which depends on your volume. A website takes one to two weeks, and the pace depends mostly on how fast you approve the copy.
